speaker: emilysangster
text: OK. Good evening, Mr. Chair and committee members. I'll start here by providing a very brief overview of the administration's review of the public participation policy. As background, the public participation policy was first prepared in 2012, updated in 2015 and ratified in 2018 by council. It was last brought to committee of the whole in March 2019 to present new changes proposed by administration, including the addition of two new guiding principles, namely shared responsibility and commitment and evaluation and continual improvement. A minor adjustment to the presentation of the roles and responsibilities in the policy, namely a nesting the project manager and communications officer bullet points under administration's role and redesigning the supporting public participation guide to reflect the city's new branding. At that time, the following discussion committee of the whole directed administration to continue to review the policy and bring it back to a future meeting. Following that, in late 2019, the public engagement community of practice was established within administration to support improved public engagement practices in Beaumont. Its terms of reference include the development of an integrated public engagement system and manual with identified processes and tools. And the public participation policy was reviewed as part of this ongoing work. There are a number of specific substantive changes between the current policy and what's proposed this evening. And I'll just go through them one by one so that they're quite clear. First, adding the shared responsibility and commitment and evaluation and continual improvement principles as was proposed in 2019. Second, combining the general public and stakeholders roles into one municipal stakeholders role under roles and responsibilities to reduce duplication and recognize that the public are in fact stakeholders. Three, removing specific position titles under administration's role, recognizing that these can change, but administration's overall responsibilities remain consistent. Fourth, adding more detailed text to introduce the public participation spectrum that is shown within the policy. This provides a bit more clarity on what the spectrum is and how it fits into Beaumont's public participation processes, and also emphasize that our processes include reporting back to the public. Fifth, adding the empower level of engagement to the spectrum, which corresponds fully to the International Association for Public Participation spectrum that is the internationally recognized source for this continuum. Six, adding a new heading on public participation processes to explicitly define the circumstances under which Beaumont will engage the public. Seventh, updating the content under the procedures heading to reference the scope of the public engagement manual that's being developed and state how it supports the policy. Also in that section we're noting that all other relevant policies and legislation also apply. Clearly state where the policy is available and also clearly state when it will be reviewed. And finally, updating some of the language and titles under the authority heading. So overall it's intended that this policy will continue to provide general authority and direction for public engagement in Beaumont, and the forthcoming manual, which we expect will be completed around the end of 2020, will provide the implementation details and procedures that can be more readily adapted, perhaps as needed, than the policy itself. So are there any questions on the revised policy before committee discusses and provides direction?

speaker: emilysangster
text: Certainly, it does, as you noted, Councillor, very tremendously by project. The general framework that's laid out in the policy is one that is, it's almost sort of the international standard for participation, set out by the International Association for Public Participation. Essentially, when implementing it with regards to a project, one of the first things that we would do would really be identify the decision that is to be made or the issue that is to be engaged on. And consider in what ways input might be used to enhance that decision or to allow us to reach a decision that is, that, you know, say is more equitable or more beneficial. We'd consider those questions, we'd consider who the stakeholders are and really work to identify those. And then based on the type of the decision to be made, the kinds of interests that we anticipate who's going to be affected, we would look to choose a level of engagement for the project that would help us gather the information or communicate the information that we need to reach the best decision possible. So depending on the scope of input that stakeholders may have for the decision, there are some decisions where, for instance, we have legislative frameworks that we have to uphold. And so there are certain things that external stakeholders and the public might not be able to influence. In those cases, you know, there may be more of a role for level, for say the informed level or the consult level where there's, you know, there's less room there, but in areas where there is more scope for the public to influence the decision, we might look at having something that is more towards consult or collaborate, where we can work more closely with stakeholders on the decision of that issue.
